Minh — thanks for the clear list. Below is the minimal evidence and allowlist we require for a standard private endpoint (Dedicated/Private mode). I'm copying our infra engineer (Jonas) and your account lead (Marissa) so we can align on schedule and DocuSign for the network annex.

Minimal allowlist (outbound from your VPC to Redwood):
- IPs (CIDR): 34.122.16.0/28, 34.122.32.0/28, 35.190.88.0/29 (control plane & telemetry).
- FQDNs (TLS outbound to): control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, updates.redwood.ai
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS/TLS), 853 (DNS over TLS if you enforce), 443 for mTLS endpoints
- Protocols: TLS 1.2+, SNI required for control.redwood.ai; mutual TLS optional for higher assurance (we can provide cert CNs if you prefer).

Evidence we ask you to upload:
- Signed network diagram showing CIDR boundaries and NAT egress (PDF)
- Screenshot of firewall rules after they are applied (or an export)
- Short note (1 paragraph) naming the owner of the egress rule (team/person) and scheduled rotation policy for ephemeral IPs
- If you use a proxy/egress gateway, include its IP and hostname and whether it rewrites SNI

No inbound holes are required for normal operation — Redwood uses outbound-only connections from your VPC to our control plane. If you plan to use a VPN-based direct connect for private traffic, we will call that out separately.

Jonas — can you confirm the control-plane IP set and whether we should ask for DNS allowlisting (resolved FQDNs) in addition to IPs? Also attaching our allowlist_template.csv for their ops team to fill.

Laura Bennett

Thanks Laura — adding a few implementation details from the infra side so your network team can implement rules with minimal back-and-forth.

Technical notes (implementation guidance):
- We publish the full control-plane IP range and a signed digest weekly. For onboarding use the three /28s above; once provisioned we'll give you a stable set tied to your tenant.
- DNS: we recommend allowlisting control.redwood.ai via DNS in addition to IPs because we leverage cloud autoscaling. If your firewall supports FQDN/URL rules, add control.redwood.ai and telemetry.redwood.ai.
- SNI: SNI is required for routing inside our edge; some TLS-inspecting proxies will break SNI. If you have a proxy that terminates TLS (and re-issues), please either: (a) configure passthrough for these hosts, or (b) provide the proxy CA cert and confirm it preserves the original SNI.
- mTLS: optional. If you need stronger auth, we can provision a client cert for your egress gateway and you'll need to present that to control.redwood.ai on port 443.
- Outbound DNS resolution: ensure your resolver can resolve our *.redwood.ai records (we recommend allowing outbound DNS to 8.8.8.8 or your managed DNS; DNS over TLS to 1.1.1.1:853 also works).
- Telemetry: telemetry.redwood.ai accepts aggregated metrics over HTTPS on 443. If you use an egress proxy, verify that it forwards POST bodies > 16KB (some proxies truncate large telemetry batches).

Evidence checklist (ops-friendly):
1) edison_network_diagram_v1.pdf (signed by network owner)
2) allowlist_template.csv (populated with final egress IPs you configured)
3) firewall-rule-export.txt (showing rules with timestamps)
4) short owner statement: "Network egress owned by <team> / rotation cadence monthly"

Note: We do not require ASN evidence for standard cases, but if you're providing a dedicated NAT IP range under a transit ASN, include the ASN in the network diagram.

Jonas Weber
Infra Engineer, Runtime Networking
Redwood Inference

--
